source.title: TabDPT: Scaling Tabular Foundation Models on Real Data
source.authors: Junwei Ma; Valentin Thomas; Rasa Hosseinzadeh; Alex Labach; Hamidreza Kamkari; Jesse C. Cresswell; Keyvan Golestan; Guangwei Yu; Anthony L. Caterini; M. Volkovs

record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling behavior in tabular foundation models, a modality outside text pretraining.
record.gate_note: Section 4.5 reports a scaling sweep and fitted power law for TabDPT. The downstream benchmark comparisons, ablations, and few-shot results do not separately test a claim version about scaling.
record.test_reason: Section 4.5 trains TabDPT tabular transformers across 33K–78M parameters and 52M–2B cells of real data. It fits a Hoffmann-style joint power law (Eq. 2), giving α=0.42 and β=0.39, which bears on V5 (power-law form outside text pretraining).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that TabDPT shows power-law scaling, with consistent gains from larger models and more real pretraining data, analogous to LLMs and other foundation models.
record.recipe_differences: This is a tabular-model scaling sweep using a joint fit to model parameters and cell count, with a mixed classification/regression metric; it is not a language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling experiment.
record.problems: The scaling metric combines classification cross-entropy with 1 − ρ for regression rather than measuring language-model held-out cross-entropy. The reported exponents have no uncertainty stated, and the study does not test extrapolation to runs substantially larger than the fitted runs or compute-optimal allocation.

untested.parts: Image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes. Only tabular in-context-learning pretraining with SSL on real data is tested.
No held-out extrapolation of a small-run fit to larger runs.
Depth and width are co-varied, not tested at fixed parameter count.
Downstream accuracy is not related to model or data scale.
No comparison of fitting choices; a single fit method (Besiroglu et al.) is used.

record.verdict_notes: The loss metric is a mean of classification cross-entropy and 1−ρ for regression, not a pure cross-entropy. Figure 4b (real vs synthetic training curves) and Figure 3b (context size vs accuracy) are not scaling-law tests. Few-shot and benchmark results are not relevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: The study concerns tabular models, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
It fits a scaling curve but does not report a test where a fit on small runs predicts the loss of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute budget or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is evaluated.
The study varies model size by changing both layer count and dimensions; it does not test the effect of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests tabular models trained with real data and SSL. It does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
It does not report downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
It does not systematically vary fitting choices or report curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: TabDPT
rows.stage_stated: Pre-training on real tabular data with self-supervised learning
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size and pre-training data amount and fitted a joint power-law scaling model.

conditions.value: mean of classification cross-entropy loss and 1 − ρ for regression

rows.measure: Joint power-law fit to excess loss; reported scaling exponents α = 0.42 and β = 0.39.
rows.value: α = 0.42; β = 0.39; the study reports consistent improvements as model and data size increase.
rows.note: The plotted loss is the mean of classification cross-entropy and 1 − ρ for regression; the figure displays excess loss after subtracting E. Results are reported for the scaling sweep as a whole, not separately for each model size or data amount.
rows.check: Row is correctly linked. The values are fitted exponents; no fit residuals or uncertainty are given. The plot shows excess loss after subtracting the fitted E, which favours a power-law look. The evaluation set for the loss is not stated. The data range spans under two orders of magnitude (52M–2B cells); parameters span about 3.4 orders.

relationships.condition: TabDPT tabular transformers pretrained with SSL on real OpenML data, 33K–78M params, 52M–2B cells
relationships.reason: The joint power-law fit (α=0.42, β=0.39) tracks the loss, with consistent gains in both model and data size (r1). No goodness-of-fit or uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: A joint power law with α=0.42 and β=0.39 tracked loss improvements from model and data scaling, without reported goodness-of-fit or uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
